conditions.quote: urgent attention to the patient with a new stroke
conditions.note: A new stroke suspected from sudden-onset symptoms (the possible-stroke rule) is treated as "a new stroke". Alternative: list the sudden-onset findings directly (same effect).

elements_not_encoded.text: If oxygen saturation < 94% or respiratory rate ≥ 30, give face mask oxygen.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Oxygen therapy instruction; SpO2 and RR are routine vitals, not a triage criterion on this page.

elements_not_encoded.text: Keep patient nil by mouth until swallowing is formally assessed.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Nil by mouth until swallowing assessed: management.
Glucose check and hypoglycaemia pointer (19): management; glucose is a routine vital, hypoglycaemia is handled on page 19.

elements_not_encoded.text: Avoid treating BP ≥ 140/90 as this may worsen stroke. If BP ≥ 220/120, discuss with specialist about need for pre-referral treatment.
elements_not_encoded.reason: BP management advice (avoid treating; discuss if >= 220/120): not a triage criterion.

If patient can reach hospital within 3 hours of onset of symptoms, refer urgently for thrombolysis to specialist stroke unit (if available).

judgment_calls.decision: Urgent, as the red box says "Give urgent attention".
judgment_calls.alternatives: Very urgent, matching the Focal neurology warning sign level (that sign fires Very urgent independently anyway).

judgment_calls.decision: No TIA diagnosis rule; "lasted < 24 hours and resolved completely" cannot be expressed. A new TIA is checked for and makes the patient Urgent.
